distractors.reason: We don't say 'much quiet'. 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns or verbs: much time, I don't like it much.
We don't say 'many quiet'. 'Many' is used with plural countable nouns: many students.
We don't say 'lots quiet'. 'Lots' is used as a noun phrase: lots of students, not before an adjective.

l1_interference: Os falantes de português costumam usar 'much' ou 'many' porque 'muito' serve para tudo. Em inglês, antes de um adjetivo usamos 'very': 'very quiet', não 'much quiet'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the standard degree adverb placed before an adjective to show a high level of a quality: very quiet, very good, very big.
memory_tip: VERY + adjective (very quiet, very good) | MUCH + verb or noun (I like it very much, much time)
